Cricket Pest Control: How to Stop Indoor Infestations

By Shaw's Pest Control  ·  Wichita, KS

What's the Best Way to Handle Cricket Pest Control in Your Home?

If you're hearing chirping in your basement or finding crickets hopping across your kitchen floor, you're dealing with one of the most common fall pest problems in Kansas homes. Cricket pest control isn't just about killing the bugs you see—it's about understanding why they're coming inside and stopping them at the source. In Wichita and across the region, September through November brings massive cricket migrations as temperatures drop and these insects search for warmth and moisture. At Shaw's Pest Control, we've been helping Kansas families deal with cricket invasions since 1987, and our Master Tech–certified team knows exactly what works (and what doesn't). This guide will walk you through the two main cricket species you're likely dealing with, why your home is attracting them, and the treatment methods that actually deliver lasting results.

Why Crickets Invade Kansas Homes Every Fall

Crickets don't come inside because they're looking for food—they're fleeing cold weather and seeking shelter. As nighttime temperatures in Kansas dip into the 50s and 40s, field crickets and camel crickets instinctively move toward heated structures. Your home's foundation, exterior lighting, and landscaping all play a role in how attractive your property is to these pests.

Field crickets are the classic brown or black crickets you see hopping around outdoor lights. They're drawn to bright outdoor lighting at night and will congregate by the hundreds near doorways, garages, and window wells. Once they find a crack or gap in your foundation, weatherstripping, or door threshold, they'll squeeze inside. These are the crickets that chirp—only the males do this, and they're incredibly persistent once they set up inside a wall void or basement.

Camel crickets (sometimes called cave crickets or spider crickets) are a different story. These humpbacked, silent crickets prefer dark, damp spaces like crawl spaces, basement window wells, and unfinished storage areas. They don't chirp, but they do reproduce quickly in the right conditions. Camel crickets are also strong jumpers, which startles most homeowners when they encounter them. Both species can become a serious nuisance when populations explode, and that's when most people realize they need professional pest control in Wichita or surrounding areas.

What Actually Stops Crickets: Treatment Methods That Work

There's a big difference between killing the crickets you see and solving the problem long-term. Sticky traps and indoor sprays might catch a few crickets, but they don't address the source—the population living just outside your foundation or the entry points letting them in.

The most effective cricket pest control strategy is a perimeter treatment combined with exclusion work. A liquid residual insecticide applied around your home's foundation, door frames, garage edges, and window wells creates a barrier that kills crickets on contact and repels new ones for weeks. This is the same approach we use at Shaw's Pest Control, and it's backed by our three state certifications and decades of fieldwork in Kansas conditions.

But treatment alone isn't enough. If your home has gaps under doors, cracks in foundation walls, torn window screens, or improperly sealed vents, crickets will keep finding ways inside. Exclusion means sealing those entry points—door sweeps, caulking gaps, repairing weatherstripping, and screening vents. These aren't glamorous fixes, but they're what separate a temporary fix from a lasting solution.

Indoor treatments with a vacuum, glue traps, or targeted spray can help manage crickets that are already inside, but they won't stop the next wave. If you're dealing with camel crickets in a damp basement or crawl space, you'll also need to address moisture issues—dehumidifiers, better ventilation, and fixing leaks all make your home less hospitable to these moisture-loving pests.

When to Call a Professional for Cricket Control

Most homeowners can manage a few stray crickets with a shoe and some patience. But when you're hearing constant chirping, finding crickets in multiple rooms, or dealing with camel crickets reproducing in your crawl space, it's time to bring in a professional. DIY sprays from the hardware store often use lower-concentration products that don't last, and improper application can leave gaps in coverage that crickets will exploit.

A licensed pest control provider has access to professional-grade materials, knows where to apply them for maximum effectiveness, and can identify the conditions that are drawing crickets to your property in the first place. If you're in Derby, for example, cricket pressure can be especially intense near the undeveloped fields south of town—that's when proactive pest control in Derby makes the difference between a quiet home and a noisy infestation.

Professional treatment also includes follow-up service. Cricket migrations can last weeks, and a single treatment in early September might not carry you through the entire fall season. Many providers, including Shaw's, offer seasonal pest control plans that include cricket suppression as part of a broader pest control strategy.

Cricket Problems in Wichita and the Surrounding Area

Wichita's mix of urban development and open prairie makes it a hotspot for cricket activity every fall. The city's relatively mild early autumn and proximity to agricultural land mean that cricket populations build throughout the summer and then surge toward homes and businesses as temperatures drop. Neighborhoods near undeveloped land, golf courses, or parks tend to see the heaviest activity.

If you live in El Dorado, Andover, Augusta, Haysville, Maize, or Goddard, you're dealing with the same seasonal patterns. Crickets don't respect city limits—they follow temperature gradients and light sources. The good news is that with the right approach, you can keep them outside where they belong. That starts with a thorough inspection of your home's exterior and a targeted treatment plan that addresses your property's specific risk factors.

Frequently Asked Questions

What attracts crickets to my house?

Crickets are attracted to outdoor lighting, warmth, moisture, and shelter. Bright lights near doors and windows draw field crickets at night, while damp basements and crawl spaces attract camel crickets. Once crickets gather near your home's foundation, they'll exploit cracks, gaps, and open thresholds to get inside. Reducing outdoor lighting, fixing moisture problems, and sealing entry points all help reduce cricket pressure.

How do I get rid of crickets in my basement?

Remove crickets in your basement by vacuuming up visible insects, setting glue traps along walls and corners, and addressing moisture issues with a dehumidifier or better ventilation. For long-term cricket pest control, treat the exterior foundation with a residual insecticide and seal cracks or gaps where crickets are entering. If camel crickets are reproducing in your basement, you'll need to eliminate damp conditions they thrive in.

What's the difference between field crickets and camel crickets?

Field crickets are the dark brown or black crickets that chirp and are attracted to light. They're usually found near doors, garages, and window wells. Camel crickets are tan or mottled, don't chirp, have a hunched back, and prefer dark, moist environments like crawl spaces and basements. Both invade homes in the fall, but they require slightly different control approaches based on their behavior and habitat preferences.

Do crickets cause damage to homes?

Crickets generally don't cause structural damage, but they can be a serious nuisance. Field crickets chirp constantly, which disrupts sleep and creates stress. Large populations can soil surfaces with fecal matter, and camel crickets may chew on fabric, paper, or cardboard in storage areas. The bigger issue is that a cricket infestation often signals entry points that other pests—like spiders, mice, or beetles—can also exploit.

How long does professional cricket treatment last?

Professional cricket pest control treatments typically provide 30 to 90 days of protection, depending on weather conditions, cricket pressure, and the products used. Residual insecticides break down over time due to rain, sun, and temperature fluctuations. For season-long control during fall cricket migrations, most pest control providers recommend a treatment in late August or early September, with a follow-up in October if needed.

Can I prevent crickets without using pesticides?

You can reduce cricket problems with exclusion and habitat modification—sealing cracks, installing door sweeps, reducing outdoor lighting, and eliminating moisture sources all help. However, during heavy migration periods in Kansas, exclusion alone often isn't enough to stop determined crickets. A targeted exterior pesticide treatment combined with exclusion work provides the most reliable long-term cricket pest control without needing to spray indoors.
